summary: Add a canvases resource: create, read, edit, delete, access-set, and section lookup.
reason: The Slack spec this CLI was generated from carries no canvas endpoints, so the generator emitted no canvas commands at all — the entire surface was missing rather than broken. Canvases are a primary Slack content type, and their absence was the main reason users had to keep the Slack MCP connector alongside this CLI. Six endpoints are wired: canvases.create, canvases.edit, canvases.delete, canvases.access.set, canvases.sections.lookup, and conversations.canvases.create for channel-bound canvases. Requires the canvases:write and canvases:read user-token scopes; without them Slack answers missing_scope, which checkSlackAPIError already renders with the scope name and reinstall hint. Structured as one file behind a shared postCanvas helper rather than the generated one-file-per-command layout: six copies of the client/error/envelope boilerplate would be harder to review and keep consistent, and since no template produces these commands there is no generated output for a reprint to diff against. Argument validation is done locally where Slack would otherwise answer a bare invalid_arguments — the operation enum, the access level, and which operations require --section or content — because an unhelpful error on a six-operation edit API is a usability trap. --content-file is offered alongside --content since canvas bodies are usually authored as Markdown files rather than typed inline. Reading is handled separately because Slack exposes no get-canvas-content endpoint. A canvas is backed by a file, so files.info's url_private_download serves the document body as HTML — the technique third-party tooling uses, but reachable with a plain xoxp OAuth token and files:read rather than the browser-session (xoxc/xoxd) credentials those tools extract from Slack Desktop's local storage. That mattered enough to verify directly: the OAuth path works, so the CLI does not need to scrape session credentials. The returned HTML carries section ids inline, which makes 'canvases read' strictly more useful than 'canvases sections' for targeting edits — sections.lookup returns ids with no content, so pairing an id to the text it covers previously required guessing. A new client.FetchRaw handles the download: files.slack.com is a different host serving non-JSON, so do()'s path joining and envelope handling do not apply. It refuses non-Slack hosts and non-https schemes, because unlike the upload URL in files_upload.go this request does carry the workspace credential and the URL comes from an API response rather than from the operator.
validated_outcome: Full lifecycle verified against a live workspace. The API contract was first established endpoint by endpoint with direct calls, then exercised through the commands: create from a --content-file Markdown document returned a canvas_id; canvases sections found both h2 sections; insert_at_end raised the h2 count from 2 to 3; insert_after against a looked-up section id succeeded; access-set with --access-level write succeeded; and both test canvases were removed with canvases delete. A channel canvas was created via conversations.canvases.create against a DM, confirming the channel path works and that DMs are accepted. Nine validation paths each produce a named error: invalid --operation, delete without --section, replace without --section, insert_at_end without content, invalid --access-level, access-set with neither --users nor --channels, channel canvas without content, --content with --content-file, and delete without --canvas. Slack rejections surface as errors and exit 5. --title against a channel canvas warns on stderr rather than silently ignoring the flag. go build, go vet, gofmt and go test ./internal/cli/ all clean. Every canvas created during verification was deleted afterwards and the workspace canvas list confirmed to contain nothing from the test date. Reading verified end to end: a canvas created with a known marker string read back through both --format html and --format text with the marker and all list items intact. The read-to-edit round trip was demonstrated by extracting a section id from the read output, targeting it with insert_after, and reading back to confirm the insert landed immediately after that heading rather than elsewhere. canvases_amend_test.go adds 12 cases: five for the HTML-to-text conversion (headings, list items, attribute values not leaking as text, blank-run collapsing, empty input) and seven for FetchRaw's host guard, including the suffix-confusion hosts slack.com.evil.example.com and files.slack.com.attacker.net plus plaintext http, alongside the two legitimate Slack hosts. All pass.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: Canvas endpoints in the Slack spec catalog
deferred_to_upstream.reason: The spec predates canvases and has no entry for any of the six endpoints, so a reprint would drop this resource entirely. Adding them to the catalog is the durable fix; this patch is a local stopgap until then.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: Nested-object body parameters in the generated command template
deferred_to_upstream.reason: Canvas endpoints take structured bodies — document_content{type,markdown} and changes[]{operation,document_content,section_id} — while the generated body builder maps flat scalar flags to top-level keys. Even with the endpoints in the catalog, the current template could not express these shapes, so canvas commands would need hand-writing regardless.

notes: Canvas content reads back as HTML, not the Markdown it was created from, so create/read is not a lossless round trip. --format text is a deliberately crude tag strip for grepping; anything needing structure should read the HTML, which is also where the section ids live. The Slack MCP connector is no longer required for canvases.
